name: Minority protection

subjectOf.text: Courts have recognized an enhanced fiduciary duty among participants in closely held corporations, holding that majority shareholders owe fiduciary duties not only to the corporation but to minority shareholders as a class.
subjectOf.abstract: The distinct needs of close corporations is also shown as courts have recognized an enhanced fiduciary duty among participants in closely held corporations.64 Courts have held that majority shareholders have a fiduciary duty not only to the corporation but also to minority shareholders as a class
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Shareholder Agreements - National Report of the United States of America (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3017612

subjectOf.text: Contractual consent to a cash out does not extinguish fiduciary claims: a minority shareholder who agreed to receive cash for shares may still challenge the merger as a breach of fiduciary duty.
subjectOf.abstract: The merger agreement allowed the company to give the minority shareholder cash in exchange for shares, but the Third Circuit determined that even if a minority shareholder agrees to a cash out, he may still object to the merger on grounds of a breach of fiduciary duty.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Shareholder Agreements - National Report of the United States of America (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3017612
scope_conditions: merger structured to eliminate a minority shareholder
Third Circuit in Coleman v. Taub

subjectOf.text: The governance rules of the DAO can be set up so as to ensure that minority token holders are appropriately protected.
subjectOf.abstract: The governance rules of the DAO can be set up so as to ensure that minority token holders are appropriately protected.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Decentralized Underwriting (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396542

subjectOf.text: Majority rule in a microdemocracy can produce discrimination, because a majority that is itself unaffected by a rule it enacts can impose a disproportionate burden on the minority the rule does affect.
subjectOf.abstract: Similarly, majority rule may mean discrimination of the minority. A majority that is unaffected by a rule they instantiate may have a discriminatory impact on a minority that is disproportionately affected by the change in the rules.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Blockchain Technology for Good (2020). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3709041
scope_conditions: applies to majority rule voting in microdemocratic systems

subjectOf.text: Fundamental rule changes in a large decentralized organization are typically demanded when a large minority is treated unfairly, which means the advantaged majority has no incentive to make the change; the resulting deadlock leaves revolution or a network split as the only route to foundational change.
subjectOf.abstract: When a large decentralized organization needs a fundamental rule change, it of- ten happens because a large minority subgroup is being treated unfairly. That typically means the majority is advantaged by the rules and are therefore not incentivized to change the rules.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Governance (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782214

subjectOf.text: Majority rule in microdemocratic systems can produce discrimination against minorities, because a majority that is itself unaffected by a rule it instantiates can impose a discriminatory impact on a minority that is disproportionately affected.
subjectOf.abstract: Similarly, majority rule may mean discrimination of the minority. A majority that is unaffected by a rule they instantiate may have a discriminatory impact on a minority that is disproportionately affected by the change in the rules.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How Decentralized Systems Can Upgrade AI (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808867
